correctness.rationale: For arbitrary n>1 with positive prime exponents alpha_i and L=lcm(alpha_i), each alpha_i divides L and gcd(k,alpha_i)=gcd(gcd(k,L),alpha_i); totient counts gcd(k,L)=d are phi(L/d). Exact least period follows because equality f(L-T)=f(L)=sum alpha_i for hypothetical 0<T<L forces alpha_i|(L-T) for every i and hence L|(L-T), impossible. Extremal fibers follow from gcd bounds, and the mean from sum_{k=1}^a gcd(k,a)=sum_{d|a}(a/d)phi(d). Independent exact integer cross-check covered 216 triples of exponent values 1..6; the all-n proof is symbolic, not finite inference.

evidence: Bouderbala–Karras Theorem 2.2: L is a period; Theorem 2.4 a sufficient equality condition.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A general elementary gcd-sum identity gives the claimed mean, so it is not independently novel in isolation; the combination with all exact fibers and exact least period was not found as a stronger published result.
